/admin-guide/use-without-admin.summary: Explains how to manage Typemill without the admin interface by rebuilding the navigation cache manually, automatically, or via API. It covers auto-refresh navigation, cache-clearing endpoints, and deleting cache files directly.

/developer-basics/tech-overview.title: Tech Overview
/developer-basics/tech-overview.summary: Explains Typemill’s core tech stack, including PHP, Slim, Twig, Vue.js, Tailwind, and Tachyons, plus supporting libraries for Markdown, events, ACL, and validation. Also notes that dependencies are managed with Composer and that Typemill avoids JS package managers and build tools for most frontend assets.

/developer-basics/folder-overview.title: Folder Overview
/developer-basics/folder-overview.summary: Explains the Typemill folder structure, including where cached files, content, media, settings, system code, plugins, and themes are stored. Also notes the main subfolders and file types used for content, user data, and uploaded media.

/developer-basics/content.title: Content
/developer-basics/content.summary: Explains Typemill’s flat-file content structure, where Markdown files store text, YAML files store metadata, and media lives in the /media folder. It also describes how pages and folders are organized hierarchically, including folder content via index files and numeric prefixes to control ordering.

/theme-developers/intro.title: Intro
/theme-developers/intro.summary: Introduces Typemill theme development and explains that themes are built with Twig, YAML, CSS, HTML, and JavaScript, with a recommendation to use the new developer kit and Dev Theme guide. It also outlines what themes can do and the frontend knowledge expected to get started.

/theme-developers/quick-start.title: Quick Start
/theme-developers/quick-start.summary: Provides a quick start for creating a Typemill theme, including using the developer kit, locating themes in the `theme` folder, and selecting them in the author panel. It also outlines the minimal required theme files and how to define theme metadata and settings in `themeName.yaml`.

/theme-developers/theme-structure.title: Theme Structure
/theme-developers/theme-structure.summary: Explains that Typemill themes have no fixed structure beyond a few required files: index.twig, 404.twig, a theme YAML file, and preview images. It also gives naming rules and an example of an extended Twig-based theme folder layout with CSS, JS, images, pages, and partials.

/theme-developers/configuration-file.title: Theme Configuration
/theme-developers/configuration-file.summary: Explains how to create a Typemill theme configuration YAML file with required basic metadata and optional settings, admin forms, page-specific tabs, and CSP entries. Also notes how to add a PayPal donation button to the theme configuration.

/theme-developers/twig.title: Twig
/theme-developers/twig.summary: Introduces Twig as a fast, secure templating engine and explains why it’s useful for cleaner, less error-prone templates. Also covers the basic Twig syntax for printing variables and running statements like loops in TypeMill.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/home.title: home
/theme-developers/theme-variables/home.summary: Explains the Twig variable `home`, which returns `true` on the homepage and `false` on subpages. Includes an example of using it to conditionally render different templates.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/conten.title: content
/theme-developers/theme-variables/conten.summary: Explains that the Twig variable `{{ content }}` contains the full HTML content of a Markdown file and shows basic usage examples. Notes that Twig filters like `striptags` can manipulate the output, though plugins or shortcodes are usually better for more advanced content changes.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/title.title: title
/theme-developers/theme-variables/title.summary: Explains the Twig `{{ title }}` variable, which returns the first `<h1>` in a content file as plain text or falls back to the file name. Shows how to use it in an HTML `<title>` tag and with Twig filters like `title`.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/baseur.title: baseurl
/theme-developers/theme-variables/baseur.summary: Explains that the Twig variable `{{ base_url }}` provides the site’s base URL for building absolute links, especially for CSS and JS assets. For homepage links, it recommends using the separate `home url` variable instead.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/homeur.title: homeurl
/theme-developers/theme-variables/homeur.summary: Explains the Twig variable `{{ home_url }}`, which provides the site base URL or current project URL for building home links. Includes an example of using it for a logo link and notes that admins can change its behavior in project settings.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/metata.title: metatabs
/theme-developers/theme-variables/metata.summary: Explains the `metatabs` Twig variable, which exposes page meta information stored in content YAML for use in themes and meta tags. It also shows how plugins and themes can extend metatabs with additional tabs and fields.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/image.title: image
/theme-developers/theme-variables/image.summary: Explains the Twig `image` variable, which provides the lead image URL and alt text for an article, falling back from hero image to first content image to logo if needed. Includes examples for using it as a header image or in social media meta tags.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/breadc.title: breadcrumb
/theme-developers/theme-variables/breadc.summary: Explains the Twig `{{ breadcrumb }}` variable, which provides the page’s breadcrumb trail as a one-dimensional array of item objects. Shows how to loop through the breadcrumb and render links using each item’s available properties.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/item.title: item
/theme-developers/theme-variables/item.summary: Explains the Twig `{{ item }}` variable, which represents the current page item and exposes properties like title, URL, slug, and chapter data. It also shows how to use `item` for folder-based navigations and article listings, noting some properties apply only to folders.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/naviga.title: navigation
/theme-developers/theme-variables/naviga.summary: Describes the Twig `{{ navigation }}` variable, which provides the full content folder structure as a multidimensional array of item objects for building global navigation. It includes nearly all item-object data except paging fields like `thisChapter`, `nextItem`, and `prevItem`.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/settin.title: settings
/theme-developers/theme-variables/settin.summary: Describes the Twig `settings` variable in Typemill, which provides system, theme, and plugin settings for use in templates. Shows how to access built-in values like title, author, and language, as well as specific theme/plugin settings by name.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/logo.title: logo
/theme-developers/theme-variables/logo.summary: Describes the Twig `logo` variable, which contains the relative URL of the uploaded logo or `false` if no logo is configured. Shows how to conditionally display the logo image or fall back to the site title.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/curren.title: currentpage
/theme-developers/theme-variables/curren.summary: Describes the Twig variable `currentpage`, which returns the current page number for valid paginated URLs like `/p/2`, or `false` when no valid pagination exists. Pagination is only valid for folders containing posts and pages that map to an existing page.

/theme-developers/theme-variables/widget.title: widgets
/theme-developers/theme-variables/widget.summary: Describes the Twig `widgets` variable, which contains HTML snippets injected by plugins and returns `false` when no widgets are available. Includes an example of looping through widgets in a theme to render them in a widgetized area.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.title: renderMeta
/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.summary: `assets.renderMeta()` adds Typemill’s standard meta tags to a theme, including Open Graph and optional admin-defined tags like favicon, noindex, and Twitter image data. Title, description, and canonical tags are not added automatically and must be added manually, while plugin methods like `getMeta()` and `addMeta()` can be used to manage meta tags.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.title: renderCSS
/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.summary: Describes the Twig function `assets.renderCSS()` for outputting plugin CSS references and inline CSS. Recommends placing it after your theme stylesheets and before the closing `</head>` tag, ideally inside a Twig block.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.title: renderJS
/theme-developers/theme-functions/render.summary: Explains how to use Twig’s `assets.renderJS()` function to output JavaScript references and inline scripts from plugins. Recommends placing it near the end of the page inside a `javascripts` block before the closing `body` tag.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/activa.title: activateAxios
/theme-developers/theme-functions/activa.summary: Describes the Twig function `assets.activateAxios()` for adding and initializing Axios in a theme with the base URL and a `tmaxios` helper. Includes an example of making API requests with the initialized client.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/activa.title: activateVue
/theme-developers/theme-functions/activa.summary: Explains how to use the Twig function `{{ assets.activateVue() }}` to add the Vue library to a theme. Includes a basic example of placing it in the `javascripts` block before loading a Vue app script.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpag.title: getPageMeta
/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpag.summary: Describes the Twig function `getPageMeta(settings, pageItem)`, which returns a page’s metadata as an array for use in templates. It’s useful for listing meta information like titles and descriptions from pages in a folder or navigation.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpag.title: getPageList
/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpag.summary: Describes the Twig function `getPageList()` for retrieving a folder item by relative URL, using navigation and base URL as inputs. It is mainly used to list content from another folder, such as showing news posts on a homepage.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpro.title: getProjectsHome
/theme-developers/theme-functions/getpro.summary: Describes the Twig function `getProjectsHome(settings)`, which returns metadata for project start pages so they can be listed on a homepage or other page. Includes the required `settings` parameter, the array return value, and an example of looping through projects to display titles, descriptions, and links.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/markdo.title: markdown
/theme-developers/theme-functions/markdo.summary: Describes the Twig `markdown()` function, which converts a markdown string into HTML for use in theme settings and other template content. Includes the required string parameter, HTML return value, and an example of rendering markdown from a textarea setting.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/image-.title: image resize
/theme-developers/theme-functions/image-.summary: Describes the Twig `assets.image(...).resize(width, height).src()` method for resizing or cropping images on the fly, with examples for setting width, height, or both. It explains the required image path parameter, optional dimensions, and that the resized image is returned as a relative URL stored under `/media/custom`.

/theme-developers/theme-functions/image-.title: image grayscale
/theme-developers/theme-functions/image-.summary: Describes how to grayscale an image on the fly using the Twig `assets.image(...).grayscale().src()` function, including optional chaining with resize. The function takes a required image path and returns the relative path to the grayscaled image stored under `/media/custom`.

/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.title: develop a layout
/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.summary: Explains how to develop a custom eBook layout for the eBook plugin using YAML definitions and a Twig template, similar to Typemill themes. Lists the standard files in a layout folder, including config.yaml, cover.png, index.twig, and style.css.

/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.title: develop the yaml file
/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.summary: Explains how to create a layout YAML configuration file with basic metadata like name, copyright, and links, which is shown in the layout selection. It also shows how to define custom form fields for ebook layout settings using the `customforms` section.

/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.title: develop the twig template
/theme-developers/ebook-layouts/develop-.summary: Explains how to develop a Typemill eBook Twig template, typically based on a single `index.twig` file copied from the demo template and adapted to your needs. It also outlines the basic layout structure, including the use of paged.js, Twig, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and ebook data passed into the page.

/theme-developers/examples/create-a-full.title: Create a Full Navigation
/theme-developers/examples/create-a-full.summary: Explains how to build a full content navigation in Twig using the `navigation` variable and a recursive macro to render all levels. Also shows how to limit the navigation depth with a configurable `maxdepth` setting.

/theme-developers/examples/create-a-fold.title: Create a Folder Navigation
/theme-developers/examples/create-a-fold.summary: Explains how to build folder navigation in Twig using the `item` variable, including listing the first level of folder contents. It also shows how to recursively render all levels with a macro or move the navigation into a reusable partial.

/theme-developers/examples/list-articles.title: List Articles
/theme-developers/examples/list-articles.summary: Explains how to list articles from a Typemill folder using folderContent, optionally enriching each entry with meta information via getPageMeta. Also shows how to list articles from any folder on the site using getPageList for blog-style layouts.

/theme-developers/examples/selectable-pa.title: Selectable Page Templates
/theme-developers/examples/selectable-pa.summary: Explains how to let authors choose between multiple page templates by adding a select field to theme settings. It also shows how to conditionally include the chosen Twig template and create the corresponding template file.

/plugin-developers/intro.title: intro
/plugin-developers/intro.summary: Introduces Typemill plugins and the many ways they can extend the system, from editor features and shortcodes to routes, middleware, roles, and Twig functions. Notes that plugin development assumes solid PHP knowledge, with familiarity in OOP, namespacing, MVC, and frameworks like Slim being helpful.

/plugin-developers/quick-start.title: Quick Start
/plugin-developers/quick-start.summary: Introduces Typemill plugin development with a quick start for creating minimal PHP plugins, including the required PHP and YAML files, class structure, and event subscription pattern. Also outlines the core concepts used by plugins, such as namespaces, inheritance, events, methods, routes, and middleware, with a pointer to Vue-based plugin guides.

/plugin-developers/quick-start-with-vue.title: Quick Start with Vue
/plugin-developers/quick-start-with-vue.summary: Introduces how to add Vue applications to Typemill via its internal API, covering use cases like editor tabs, system menu items, and frontend pages. It also shows the basic PHP/YAML plugin structure needed to load Vue JavaScript and CSS into the interface.

/plugin-developers/plugin-structure.title: Plugin Structure
/plugin-developers/plugin-structure.summary: Explains the required file structure for a plugin, starting with a minimal setup of one folder plus PHP and YAML files. It also covers naming rules and how to extend the structure with additional code, templates, JavaScript, and vendor libraries for more complex plugins.

/plugin-developers/plugin-configuration.title: Plugin Configuration
/plugin-developers/plugin-configuration.summary: Explains how to create a Typemill plugin configuration YAML file with required metadata such as name, version, author, and license, plus optional donation links. Also covers defining default settings and forms so users can customize plugin behavior in the author panel.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/introdu.title: Introduction
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/introdu.summary: Explains Typemill’s event-driven plugin system and how plugins subscribe to events with getSubscribedEvents(). Also covers assigning multiple handlers with priorities and reading/manipulating event data with getData() and setData().

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onbread.title: onBreadcrumbLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onbread.summary: Describes the onBreadcrumbLoaded frontend event, which fires after a page breadcrumb is created so plugins can modify or return the breadcrumb before display. It is available on all frontend pages except the homepage, and a breadcrumb must be returned or it will not appear in the frontend.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onconte.title: onContentArrayLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onconte.summary: Describes the onContentArrayLoaded frontend event, triggered after Markdown is parsed into a content array but before it is rendered to HTML, allowing plugins to modify or insert content at specific elements. Plugins must return a content array for the page content to remain available in the frontend.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/oncsplo.title: onCspLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/oncsplo.summary: Describes the `onCspLoaded` event, which fires after plugins and themes load and lets plugins add external domains to the site’s CSP whitelist. Plugins must return and update an array of domains so third-party resources can load correctly.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onhtmll.title: onHtmlLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onhtmll.summary: Describes the onHtmlLoaded event, which fires after markdown is converted to HTML on frontend pages and lets plugins read and modify the page content. Plugins must return an HTML string, and the content passed in does not include the first H1 element.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/oniteml.title: onItemLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/oniteml.summary: Describes the onItemLoaded event, which fires after a page item is extracted from navigation and is available on frontend pages and editor pages in the author environment. Plugins must return the item object through setData/getData to avoid errors, and the page includes a PHP example of using the event to add metadata.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmarkd.title: onMarkdownLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmarkd.summary: Describes the onMarkdownLoaded event, which fires after a page’s markdown is loaded but before it is converted to HTML, allowing plugins to read or modify the markdown. It also notes availability, the required markdown string data format, and provides a plugin example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmetad.title: onMetaDefinitionsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmetad.summary: Describes the onMetaDefinitionsLoaded event, which fires after meta-data field definitions are loaded in the editor view. Plugins must return an array of meta-definitions here to enable the meta tabs, and it differs from onMetaLoaded, which provides the meta-data itself.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmetal.title: onMetaLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onmetal.summary: Describes the onMetaLoaded frontend event, which fires after page metadata is loaded and requires plugins to return the metadata array for it to be available in the frontend. Includes the event’s data structure, a PHP example, and links to related meta-definition and authoring docs.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpagec.title: onPageCreated
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpagec.summary: Describes the onPageCreated event, which fires after a page is created in the author interface and can be used to sync page-related data. It is available only for the POST /api/v2/article endpoint, provides page markdown, metadata, itempath, and username via getData, and does not support setData.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaged.title: onPageDeleted
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaged.summary: Triggered after a page is deleted in the author interface, `onPageDeleted` provides the deleted page’s item object so plugins can sync or clean up related data. It is only available for the DELETE `/api/v2/article` endpoint, and `setData` is not supported.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaged.title: onPageDiscard
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaged.summary: Describes the onPageDiscard event, which fires after a page’s changes are discarded in the author interface and can be used to sync related data. It is available only for the /api/v2/article/discard endpoint, does not support setData, and provides getData with the new markdown, username, and item.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpagep.title: onPagePublished
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpagep.summary: Triggered after a page is published in the author interface, this event provides the page’s item, username, markdown, and metadata so plugins can sync or process the published content. It is only available for the PUT /api/v2/article endpoint, and setData is not supported.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpager.title: onPageReady
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpager.summary: Describes the onPageReady event, which fires when a page is fully prepared for rendering and lets plugins add extra page data before it is shown. It applies to frontend and author editor pages, and merged data can be set via the page data array.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpager.title: onPageRenamed
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpager.summary: Describes the onPageRenamed event, which fires after a page slug is changed in the author interface and can be used to sync related data. It includes the available API endpoint, event data structure, and a PHP example for handling renamed page revisions.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpages.title: onPageSorted
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpages.summary: `onPageSorted` fires after a page is reordered in the author interface, letting plugins sync related data. It is only available for POST `/api/v2/article/sort`, and provides the old and new item via `getData` (no `setData`).

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpageu.title: onPageUnpublished
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpageu.summary: Describes the onPageUnpublished event, which fires after a page is deleted in the author interface and can be used to sync related data. It is available only for the /api/v2/article delete endpoint, provides deleted page data via getData, and does not support setData.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpageu.title: onPageUpdated
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpageu.summary: Describes the onPageUpdated event, which is available only on the PUT /api/v2/draft endpoint and provides the old and new markdown, username, and item via getData. It is intended for syncing extra data, and setData is not available.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaget.title: onPagetreeLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onpaget.summary: Triggered after the content navigation tree is built, this event lets plugins modify the navigation for the frontend or author interface. Plugins must return the navigation data, or it will not be available.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onplugi.title: onPluginsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onplugi.summary: Triggered after all active plugins have loaded, this event lets you inspect which plugins are available by reading the plugin name/class list from `getData`. It is available everywhere and does not support `setData`.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onproje.title: onProjectFound
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onproje.summary: Describes the onProjectFound event, which fires after a project is detected in the current URL when the projects feature is enabled. It provides the project ID via getData and is useful for plugins that need project-specific behavior.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onresou.title: onResourcesLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onresou.summary: Describes the onResourcesLoaded event, which fires after resource definitions load and lets plugins add or modify ACL resources. It applies everywhere and requires plugins to return a valid resource array so roles and permissions work correctly.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onroles.title: onRolesPermissionsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onroles.summary: Describes the onRolesPermissionsLoaded event, which fires after ACL roles and permissions are loaded and can be used to add or modify user roles. Plugins must return the roles-and-rights array for ACL to work correctly.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsessi.title: onSessionSegmentsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsessi.summary: Describes the onSessionSegmentsLoaded event, which runs after session URL segments are loaded and lets plugins add segments to start sessions for specific pages or integrations. It notes that plugins must return the segment array, or sessions for other plugins will not start.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsetti.title: onSettingsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsetti.summary: Describes the `onSettingsLoaded` event, which fires after all settings have been merged and loaded and is available everywhere. Plugin developers should use `getSettings` or `getPluginSettings` to access settings, since `setData` is not available for this event.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onshort.title: onShortcodeFound
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onshort.summary: Describes the onShortcodeFound event, which fires when markdown shortcodes are parsed into HTML and can be used by plugins to create or replace shortcode output. It includes the shortcode data available, notes that plugins must return replacement data for frontend availability, and shows a PHP usage example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsyste.title: onSystemnaviLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onsyste.summary: Describes the onSystemnaviLoaded event, which fires when the system navigation loads and lets plugins add or modify navigation items. Plugins must return a two-dimensional array of system navigation entries for the system view in the admin interface.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/ontwigg.title: onTwigGlobalsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/ontwigg.summary: Describes the onTwigGlobalsLoaded event, which fires early in the application lifecycle so plugins can register Twig globals for initialization in slim. Plugins must return an array of Twig globals for the event to work, and the page includes a PHP example of adding a custom global.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/ontwigl.title: onTwigLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/ontwigl.summary: Triggered when the Twig extension has loaded, this event is used to add templates, JavaScript, Vue apps, or CSS. It is available on frontend sites, author/admin interfaces, and API endpoints, and sends no data.

/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onuserf.title: onUserfieldsLoaded
/plugin-developers/plugin-events/onuserf.summary: Triggered after user fields are loaded, this event lets plugins add fields for all users or specific roles and requires returning the full content array for frontend availability. Added fields must use matching array keys and field names or validation will remove them.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addnew.title: addNewRoutes
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addnew.summary: Explains how to use the static addNewRoutes() method to register new frontend or API routes. Includes a simple PHP example mapping an HTTP method and route to a controller action.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addnew.title: addNewMiddleware
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addnew.summary: Explains how to use the `addNewMiddleware()` static method to register new middleware in Typemill. Includes a simple example returning the middleware class name and parameters.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getset.title: getSettings
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getset.summary: Explains how to use `$this->getSettings()` in a Typemill plugin to retrieve all Typemill settings as an array. Includes a simple example method showing the call inside a plugin class.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.title: getPluginSettings
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.summary: Describes the `getPluginSettings` method for retrieving a plugin’s settings from Typemill, either for a specified plugin or the currently active one by default. Includes the return type and a usage example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/storep.title: storePluginData
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/storep.summary: Explains how to use `storePluginData()` to save plugin data into a file under the plugin’s `data` folder. Includes parameter details, optional data transformation methods like `serialize` or `json_encode`, return values, and example usage.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/storep.title: storePluginYamlData
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/storep.summary: Describes how to store plugin YAML data with `$this->storePluginYamlData()`, including validation against field definitions before writing to a specified YAML file. Also notes the possible return values for success, errors, or validation failures.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.title: getPluginData
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.summary: Explains how to use getPluginData($filename) to retrieve data from a specified file in a plugin’s data folder. Includes the parameter, return value, and a PHP usage example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.title: getPluginYamlData
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getplu.summary: Retrieves YAML-formatted data from a specified file in the current plugin. Returns the parsed array if the file is found, or false otherwise.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/delete.title: deletePluginData
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/delete.summary: Describes the `deletePluginData($filename)` method for removing a file associated with the current plugin. Includes the required filename parameter and a PHP example of usage.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getdis.title: getDispatcher
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getdis.summary: Describes how `$this->getDispatcher()` returns the Symfony event dispatcher for dispatching new or existing events. The example shows using it to trigger `onTwigLoaded` so related services, like mail, become available.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/gettwi.title: getTwig
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/gettwi.summary: Describes the `getTwig()` method for retrieving the Twig environment so a plugin can load and render templates. Includes an example showing how to add a template path and render a Twig file with variables.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.title: addTwigGlobal
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.summary: Explains how to add a global variable to Twig with addTwigGlobal(), including the required onTwigGlobalsLoaded initialization step. Shows the parameters and a PHP/Twig example of exposing a class instance as a template global.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.title: addTwigFilter
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.summary: Describes how to register a custom Twig filter with `$this->addTwigFilter($name, $filter)`, including the required name and `TwigFilter` object parameters. Shows an example plugin adding a `rot13` filter and using it in a Twig template.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.title: addTwigFunction
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addtwi.summary: Adds a custom Twig function to the template environment using `$this->addTwigFunction($name, $function)`. Includes parameter details and an example of registering and calling the function in a Twig template.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addjs.title: addJS
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addjs.summary: Describes the `addJS($JS)` method for adding JavaScript file references to a page in a Typemill plugin. It also shows how to render the included scripts in the template using `{{ renderJS() }}` before the closing body tag.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addinl.title: addInlineJS
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addinl.summary: Explains how to add inline JavaScript to a page using `$this->addInlineJS($JS)` in a Typemill plugin. Shows that the injected code is rendered in the template with `{{ renderJS() }}` before the closing body tag.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addcss.title: addCSS
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addcss.summary: Describes the `addCSS($CSS)` method for adding a CSS file reference to a page, using a relative path or URL. It also notes that the included styles are rendered in templates with `{{ renderCSS() }}` in the HTML header.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addinl.title: addInlineCSS
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addinl.summary: Describes the addInlineCSS method for adding inline CSS code to a page. The CSS is rendered in the template with renderCSS(), typically placed in the HTML header.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addsvg.title: addSvgSymbol
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addsvg.summary: Describes the `addSvgSymbol($symbol)` method for adding an SVG symbol to a plugin. Includes the required string parameter and a PHP usage example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getmet.title: getMeta
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/getmet.summary: Describes the getMeta() method, which retrieves all frontend HTML meta-tag information. It returns an array of meta data and shows basic usage in a plugin method.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addmet.title: addMeta
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/addmet.summary: Describes the `addMeta($key, $meta)` method for adding HTML meta tags to the frontend. Includes parameter details and an example that adds a `noindex` robots meta tag.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/activa.title: activateAxios
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/activa.summary: Explains how to activate the Axios library in the frontend using `$this->activateAxios()` inside a plugin. It also notes that the generated script is rendered in the template with `{{ renderJS() }}` before the closing body tag.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/activa.title: activateVue
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/activa.summary: Explains how to activate Vue.js in a plugin using `$this->activateVue()`. The Vue assets are rendered in the template with `{{ renderJS() }}`, which should be placed before the closing body tag.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/markdo.title: markdownToHtml
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/markdo.summary: Converts a Markdown string to HTML using `$this->markdownToHtml($markdown)`. Returns the converted HTML string and includes a simple PHP usage example.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/genera.title: generateForm
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/genera.summary: Generates a form from a plugin’s YAML form definitions for a given route name. Returns the generated form HTML as a string on success, or false if generation fails.

/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/valida.title: validateParams
/plugin-developers/plugin-methods/valida.summary: Validates form or request parameters using field types and optional regex rules from YAML form definitions. Returns the validated values on success or false on failure, with errors added to the session automatically.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/cookie-conse.title: Cookie Consent Plugin
/plugin-developers/tutorial/cookie-conse.summary: Explains the Cookie Consent plugin, which adds a cookie banner to site pages. It contrasts the plugin with hardcoding the script into a theme, highlighting easier maintenance and admin-side configuration of banner text, colors, and enable/disable settings.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/write-the-ya.title: Write the YAML File
/plugin-developers/tutorial/write-the-ya.summary: Explains how to create a plugin YAML configuration file in the plugin root with the same name as the plugin folder, including basic metadata like name, version, author, and license. Also describes how YAML maps to arrays in TYPEMILL, how nested options use two-space indentation, and warns to use spaces instead of tabs.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/write-the-ph.title: Write the PHP File
/plugin-developers/tutorial/write-the-ph.summary: Explains how to create a TYPEMILL plugin’s main PHP file and define its plugin class with the correct namespace and base-class inheritance. It also introduces the required static `getSubscribedEvents` method that every plugin must provide.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-methods.title: Add Methods
/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-methods.summary: Explains how to implement plugin event methods by subscribing to `onSettingsLoaded` and `onTwigLoaded`, retrieving settings data from event objects, and preparing to manipulate returned data with `getData()`/`setData()`. It then introduces adding CSS and JavaScript assets and injecting initial script/template content into the theme.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/create-the-s.title: Create the Structure
/plugin-developers/tutorial/create-the-s.summary: Explains the basic folder and file structure for a TypeMill plugin, using a cookie consent plugin as an example with a matching PHP entry file, YAML config, Twig template, and public CSS/JS assets. It also outlines naming conventions and notes that the next step is creating the configuration file.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-twig-tem.title: Add Twig Template
/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-twig-tem.summary: Explains how to create a Twig template for the cookie consent initialization script instead of embedding hardcoded JavaScript directly. It also shows how to load the template through Twig in PHP so the values can later be made editable with variables.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-default-.title: Add Default Values
/plugin-developers/tutorial/add-default-.summary: Explains how to add default plugin values in TYPEMILL by defining a `settings` block in the plugin YAML file with two-space indentation. It also shows how these defaults are merged with global and user settings and accessed in the plugin via `onSettingsLoaded`.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/use-variable.title: Use Variables in Twig
/plugin-developers/tutorial/use-variable.summary: Explains how to define default plugin settings in YAML and load them in PHP so they can be passed into a Twig template. Shows how the Cookie Consent plugin renders its banner script by fetching the Twig file with the settings array.

/plugin-developers/tutorial/make-variabl.title: Make Variables Editable
/plugin-developers/tutorial/make-variabl.summary: Explains how to make plugin settings editable in the TYPEMILL UI by defining `forms` and `fields` in the plugin’s YAML configuration. Shows that field names must match default settings and gives a `select` example for a `position` setting.

/plugin-developers/examples/add-new-user.title: Add a Userrole
/plugin-developers/examples/add-new-user.summary: Explains Typemill’s ACL-based role and permission system, including how to add or modify user roles, permissions, routes, and admin resources. It also lists the default roles and shows how plugins can access role data via the `onRolesPermissionsLoaded` event.

/plugin-developers/examples/system-navig.title: Change System Navigation
/plugin-developers/examples/system-navig.summary: Describes Typemill’s default system navigation items and the access rights required to view them, noting that only account is visible to standard users. It also explains how plugins can use the `onSystemnaviLoaded` event to extend system navigation, add custom items, and restrict them by role or permission.

/plugin-developers/examples/shortcodes.title: Create a Shortcode
/plugin-developers/examples/shortcodes.summary: Explains Typemill shortcodes, which let authors insert small snippets into markdown pages using a special syntax. It shows how plugins can listen for the `onShortcodeFound` event to replace a shortcode with custom HTML and notes that shortcodes can also be registered for use in the visual editor.

/plugin-developers/examples/routes.title: Add a New Route
/plugin-developers/examples/routes.summary: Explains how to add custom TYPEMILL routes from a plugin using the `addNewRoutes()` static method, specifying the HTTP method, route path, and controller class/method. It also shows how to register multiple routes and create the corresponding plugin controller file.

/plugin-developers/examples/middleware.title: Add a New Middleware
/plugin-developers/examples/middleware.summary: Explains how to add plugin middleware in Typemill using the addNewMiddleware() method, which returns a middleware class name and optional parameters. Notes that middleware support is basic and currently limited to global middleware with fixed execution order.

/forms/introduction.title: introduction
/forms/introduction.summary: Explains how Typemill generates forms from simple YAML definitions for plugins and themes, allowing authors to configure settings, add page metadata, and create public forms. It also shows the basic `forms > fields` structure and how submitted values can be accessed in templates.

/forms/field-overview.title: field overview
/forms/field-overview.summary: Explains Typemill form fields, including the parts of a field definition, supported field types, and common attributes like required, placeholder, and validation patterns. Also shows example usage for building forms with different field types.

/forms/themes-and-plugins.title: themes and plugins
/forms/themes-and-plugins.summary: Explains how to add editable configuration forms to themes or plugins using YAML form definitions, including field setup and available field types. It also shows where saved settings are stored and how to access them in Twig templates or plugin code.

/forms/meta-tabs.title: meta tabs
/forms/meta-tabs.summary: Explains how to add custom fields or new meta-tabs for pages in Typemill using a plugin/theme YAML definition and Vue.js. It also shows how page meta is stored separately from markdown, accessed in Twig via `metatabs`, and read in plugins through the `onMetaLoaded` event.

/forms/public-forms.title: public forms
/forms/public-forms.summary: Explains how to define public forms in a Typemill plugin using YAML, with front-end generation, validation, spam protection, and CSRF handling done automatically. Also shows how admins can customize public form labels, help text, and descriptions through referenced settings fields.

/api/postman.title: Postman
/api/postman.summary: Provides a downloadable Postman testing pack for Typemill API, including a collection, runner data, and scripts. It also explains how to run multi-role authorization tests in a STAGE environment using the Collection Runner or manual requests.

/api/get-mainnavi.title: /mainnavi
/api/get-mainnavi.summary: Returns the main navigation items for the current user, with the menu contents varying by role permissions. Requires at least the "member" role and is available via GET /api/v1/mainnavi/.

/api/get-systemnavi.title: /systemnavi
/api/get-systemnavi.summary: Returns the system navigation items available to the current user, with content varying by role and permissions. Requires at least the "member" role and is accessed via GET /api/v1/systemnavi/.

/api/get-navigation.title: /navigation
/api/get-navigation.summary: Returns the full content navigation as a multidimensional array of item objects, including published pages by default and unpublished pages when `draft=true` is set. Requires member-level authorization and is available at `GET /api/v1/navigation`.

/api/get-article.title: /article/content
/api/get-article.summary: Retrieves an article’s content as an array of blocks containing each block’s id, markdown, and HTML via GET /api/v1/article/content. Requires author access and a relative url query parameter, with an optional draft flag to return the draft version.

/api/get-meta.title: /article/meta
/api/get-meta.summary: Retrieves an article’s metadata from its meta-tabs via GET /api/v1/article/meta, using a required relative url query parameter. Authorization requires at least the author role.

/api/get-item.title: /article/item
/api/get-item.summary: Describes the GET /api/v1/article/item endpoint for retrieving a specific article item by its relative URL, with author-level authorization required. Notes that it is best used when the URL is stable; otherwise, use get items to search by slug.

/api/get-items.title: /article/items
/api/get-items.summary: Retrieves one or more article items by slug via GET /api/v1/article/items. It returns an array because slugs can repeat across folders, and requires at least the author role.

/api/get-settings.title: /settings
/api/get-settings.summary: Retrieves the system settings for the application via GET /api/v1/settings/. Requires manager authorization and returns configuration details such as version, title, editor, formats, image sizes, and plugin settings.

/api/get-user-by-email.title: /users/getbymail
/api/get-user-by-email.summary: Retrieves a single user by email via GET /api/v1/users/getbyemail. Requires administrator authorization and an email query parameter.

/api/get-users-by-name.title: /users/getbynames
/api/get-users-by-name.summary: Retrieves a list of user records for the specified usernames via GET /api/v1/users/getbynames. Requires administrator authorization and a required usernames array query parameter.

/api/get-users-by-role.title: /users/getbyrole
/api/get-users-by-role.summary: Retrieves a list of users filtered by a specified user role via GET /api/v1/users/getbyrole. Requires administrator authorization and the role query parameter.
